Ticket routing observations:

- Requests concern large items from the east region, with choices typically:
  - A: standard queue
  - B: priority desk
  - C: regional office/region (wording varies)
  - Sometimes D or other truncated options.
- Option C was rejected on 9 of 10 observed tickets, including shipment, claim, invoice, and refund requests.
- One shipment request (REQ-2400, from Aisha Rossi/Field Sales) succeeded with C, but an otherwise similar shipment request (REQ-2401) and another shipment (REQ-2407) rejected C. Do not assume east-region or shipment requests route to C.
- No evidence yet identifies whether A or B is correct, nor what special condition made C valid for REQ-2400.
- Treat sender, department, urgency, and message wording as potentially relevant; avoid relying on region alone.
- Prefer A or B over C unless clear evidence supports the regional option.

Ticket routing observations:

- Requests concern large east-region items; options usually are A: standard queue, B: priority desk, C: regional office/region (sometimes truncated), with occasional D.
- Region alone does not determine routing. Request type, sender/department, urgency, wording, and intake details may matter.
- Recent evidence:
  - A accepted REQ-2412 (Regional Ops invoice), REQ-2413 (Regional Ops refund), and REQ-2414 (Client Services refund); rejected REQ-2410, REQ-2411, REQ-2415, REQ-2416, and REQ-2417.
  - C accepted REQ-2400 and REQ-2418 (Aisha Berg, Field Sales, refund; paperwork scanned, not typed); it was rejected on most earlier observations. Do not default to C.
  - B accepted REQ-2419 (Regional Ops shipment, requested before end of day).
- Possible signals, not confirmed rules:
  - Regional Ops may often fit A, but REQ-2415 (also Regional Ops) rejected A.
  - “Scanned, not typed” may correlate with C, but evidence is only one case.
  - Urgent shipment wording may correlate with B, but evidence is only one case.
  - Sender identity and department appear potentially important; similar Field Sales requests have routed differently.
- No reliable complete routing rule is established. Prefer A or B over C absent specific supporting evidence, but test against request details rather than region or item type alone.

Ticket routing observations:

- Requests concern large east-region items; options usually A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, and sometimes D. Region/item type alone does not determine routing.
- Recent outcomes:
  - A accepted REQ-2412, 2413, 2414, 2421 (Omar Berg, Regional Ops refund), and 2423 (Priya Okafor, Finance Desk invoice); rejected 2410, 2411, 2415–2417, 2420 (Sam Chen, Regional Ops invoice), and 2422 (Yuki Rossi, Partner Accounts claim).
  - B accepted 2419 (Regional Ops shipment, urgent), 2425 (Partner Accounts invoice, urgent), and 2428 (Field Sales shipment, urgent).
  - C accepted 2400 and 2418 (Aisha Berg, Field Sales refund; scanned paperwork); rejected in most other observations. Do not default to C.
  - D accepted 2426 (Yuki Rossi, Partner Accounts invoice, bounced first form) and 2427 (Omar Chen, Partner Accounts shipment, bounced first form), but rejected 2424 (Marcus Chen, Partner Accounts invoice, urgent) and 2429 (Omar Chen, Partner Accounts refund, bounced first form). D is therefore not a simple “bounced form” rule.
- Potential signals remain unconfirmed:
  - Regional Ops often fits A, but not consistently (2420 rejected; 2421 accepted; 2415 rejected).
  - Urgent/before-end-of-day wording correlates with B (2419, 2425, 2428), but not necessarily all urgent requests.
  - Scanned paperwork may correlate with C, based on one case.
  - Sender identity, department, request type, and wording appear important; similar departments/senders can route differently.
- No complete routing rule is established. Evaluate all details and avoid assuming A, B, C, or D solely from region, item type, urgency, or form history.

Ticket routing observations:

- Requests concern large east-region items; choices are usually A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, and sometimes D. Region/item type alone does not determine routing.
- Recent accepted routes:
  - A: REQ-2412–2414, 2421 (Omar Berg, Regional Ops refund), 2423 (Priya Okafor, Finance Desk invoice), and 2432 (Jonas Kim, Field Sales invoice).
  - B: 2419, 2425, 2428 (urgent requests), 2431 (Elena Haddad, Regional Ops shipment, end-of-day), 2433 (Field Sales shipment, repeated client follow-up), and 2438 (Client Services refund, end-of-day).
  - C: 2400 and 2418 (Aisha Berg, Field Sales refund; scanned paperwork).
  - D: 2426 and 2427 (Partner Accounts requests after a bounced first form).
- Rejections further show no simple rule: A rejected 2410, 2411, 2415–2417, 2420, 2422, 2435, and 2436; B rejected 2434 (Client Services refund, end-of-day); C rejected 2430 (Field Sales claim, regional-office wording) and 2439 (Client Services refund, scanned paperwork); D rejected 2424, 2429, and 2437.
- Urgency/end-of-day and repeated follow-up often favor B, but urgency is not sufficient (2434 rejected).
- Scanned paperwork does not reliably imply C: 2418 accepted, 2439 rejected. Regional-office wording also does not imply C (2430 rejected; 2432 accepted A).
- Regional Ops often fits A but can fit B; department, sender identity, request type, wording, and possibly prior-history/form details all matter.
- No complete routing rule is established. Evaluate every detail and do not default to A, B, C, or D based solely on region, item type, urgency, paperwork, or bounced-form history.

Ticket routing observations:

- East-region/large-item routing is not determined by region or request type. Consider department, sender, request type, wording, urgency, prior history, and form/details together.
- Accepted routes:
  - A: REQ-2412–2414, 2421, 2423, 2432, 2447 (Finance shipment, “same as last month”).
  - B: 2419, 2425, 2428, 2431, 2433, 2438, 2442 (Finance refund, end-of-day), 2446 (Partner Accounts shipment, repeated client follow-up).
  - C: 2400, 2418 (Field Sales refund, scanned paperwork).
  - D: 2426, 2427 (Partner Accounts after bounced first form).
- Recent rejections:
  - A rejected 2410, 2411, 2415–2417, 2420, 2422, 2435, 2436, 2440 (Client Services refund, “same as last month”), 2441, 2444, 2445, and 2448.
  - B rejected 2434 and 2449 (Partner Accounts refund, repeated follow-up).
  - C rejected 2430 and 2439.
  - D rejected 2424, 2429, 2437, and 2443 (Partner Accounts shipment, “anything missing”).
- Urgency/end-of-day and repeated follow-up often favor B, but neither is sufficient: 2434 and 2449 rejected B. “End of day” accepted B for 2442 but rejected A for 2444.
- Scanned paperwork does not reliably imply C; regional-office wording does not imply C.
- Partner Accounts does not automatically imply D or B: D succeeded for bounced-form cases, B succeeded for repeated follow-up, while D/B failed in other cases.
- No complete routing rule is established. Avoid defaulting to A, B, C, or D based on any single attribute; use accepted examples only as weak precedents.

Ticket routing observations:

- No complete rule is established. Do not route by region, request type, department, wording, urgency, or form detail alone; combine all available attributes and use precedents cautiously.
- Accepted routes:
  - A: REQ-2412–2414, 2421, 2423, 2432, 2447, 2452.
  - B: 2419, 2425, 2428, 2431, 2433, 2438, 2442, 2446, 2454, 2459.
  - C: 2400, 2418.
  - D: 2426, 2427, 2456.
- Recent new rejections:
  - B rejected 2450 (Field Sales claim, repeated follow-up).
  - A rejected 2451 (Regional Ops shipment, receipt confirmation).
  - C rejected 2453 (Field Sales shipment, scanned paperwork), 2455 (Field Sales invoice, missing-items wording), and 2457 (Regional Ops refund, regional-office wording).
  - D rejected 2458 (Regional Ops shipment, bounced first form).
- Existing rejections remain useful: A rejected many Client Services refunds and other cases; B rejected 2434 and 2449 (Partner Accounts refunds); C rejected 2430 and 2439; D rejected 2424, 2429, 2437, and 2443.
- Repeated follow-up often favors B, now confirmed for Client Services shipment and claim (2454, 2459), but not Field Sales claim (2450) or earlier Partner Accounts refunds.
- “Anything missing,” scanned paperwork, regional-office wording, bounced forms, and end-of-day are weak signals only. Notably, “anything missing” accepted A for 2452, while similar wording elsewhere failed D; bounced-form routing also varies.
- Partner Accounts regional-office claim succeeded with D (2456), but Partner Accounts cases do not automatically imply D or B.
